quickSummary: Niels Bohr applied quantum principles to single-electron species (H, He⁺, Li²⁺, Be³⁺), quantizing angular momentum (L = nℏ). The Rydberg formula quantifies all hydrogen atomic transitions across Lyman, Balmer, and infrared series.
summary: Master Bohr's postulates, parameter scaling derivations (radius, velocity, energy components), the Rydberg formula, and spectral series calculations.

summaryBox.title: Bohr Model Postulates
summaryBox.takeaway: 1. Stationary non-radiating orbits; 2. Angular momentum quantization L = m_e v r = nℏ; 3. Frequency condition ΔE = hν.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Bohr's model applies strictly to single-electron hydrogenic systems ($\text{H}, \text{He}^+, \text{Li}^{2+}, \text{Be}^{3+}$):

1. **Electrostatic = Centripetal Force**:
$$\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Z e^2}{r^2} = \frac{m_e v^2}{r} \implies m_e v^2 = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Z e^2}{r}$$

2. **Quantization of Angular Momentum**:
$$v = \frac{n h}{2\pi m_e r} = \frac{n \hbar}{m_e r}$$

3. **Bohr Radius ($r_n$)**:
$$\mathbf{r_n = \frac{\varepsilon_0 h^2}{\pi m_e e^2} \cdot \frac{n^2}{Z} = a_0 \frac{n^2}{Z} = 0.529177 \times \frac{n^2}{Z} \text{ \AA}}$$

4. **Electron Velocity ($v_n$)**:
$$\mathbf{v_n = \frac{e^2}{2\varepsilon_0 h} \cdot \frac{Z}{n} = v_1 \frac{Z}{n} = 2.188 \times 10^6 \times \frac{Z}{n} \text{ m/s}}$$

5. **Energy Components ($K_n, U_n, E_n$)**:
• **Kinetic Energy ($K_n$)**: $K_n = \frac{1}{2}m_e v^2 = +\frac{1}{8\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{Ze^2}{r_n} = \mathbf{+13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ eV}}$
• **Potential Energy ($U_n$)**: $U_n = -\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{Ze^2}{r_n} = \mathbf{-27.2 \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ eV}}$
• **Total Energy ($E_n$)**: $E_n = K_n + U_n = \mathbf{-K_n = \frac{U_n}{2} = -13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ eV/atom}}$

$$\mathbf{E_n = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ J/atom} = -1312 \times \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ kJ/mol}}$$

conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Hydrogen Emission Spectrum & Rydberg Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HYDROGEN ATOMIC TRANSITIONS
                       
   E (eV)
    0.00 ─── n = ∞ ───────────────────────────────────────────
   -0.54 ─── n = 5 ─── Pfund Series (n₁ = 5, Far IR)
   -0.85 ─── n = 4 ─── Brackett Series (n₁ = 4, Mid IR)
   -1.51 ─── n = 3 ─── Paschen Series (n₁ = 3, Near IR)
   -3.40 ─── n = 2 ─── Balmer Series (n₁ = 2, VISIBLE)
   
  -13.60 ─── n = 1 ─── Lyman Series (n₁ = 1, ULTRAVIOLET)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Transition between quantum states $n_2 \rightarrow n_1$ ($n_2 > n_1$):

$$\mathbf{\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2 \left( \frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2} \right)}$$

where $R_H = \frac{m_e e^4}{8 \varepsilon_0^2 h^3 c} \approx \mathbf{109677\text{ cm}^{-1} = 1.09677 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}}$.

**Spectral Series Classifications**:
• **Lyman ($n_1 = 1, n_2 = 2,3,4\dots$)**: Ultraviolet (UV). $\lambda_{\min} = \frac{1}{R_H} \approx 912\text{ \AA}$.
• **Balmer ($n_1 = 2, n_2 = 3,4,5,6\dots$)**: Visible ($n_2=3,4,5,6$) & Near UV. $\lambda_{\min} = \frac{4}{R_H} \approx 3646\text{ \AA}$.
• **Paschen ($n_1 = 3, n_2 = 4,5,6\dots$)**: Near Infrared (NIR). $\lambda_{\min} = \frac{9}{R_H} \approx 8206\text{ \AA}$.
• **Brackett ($n_1 = 4, n_2 = 5,6,7\dots$)**: Mid Infrared (MIR). $\lambda_{\min} = \frac{16}{R_H} \approx 14588\text{ \AA}$.
• **Pfund ($n_1 = 5, n_2 = 6,7,8\dots$)**: Far Infrared (FIR). $\lambda_{\min} = \frac{25}{R_H} \approx 22793\text{ \AA}$.
• **Humphreys ($n_1 = 6, n_2 = 7,8,9\dots$)**: Far Infrared (FIR). $\lambda_{\min} = \frac{36}{R_H} \approx 32823\text{ \AA}$.

• **Total Emission Lines**: $N = \frac{(n_2 - n_1)(n_2 - n_1 + 1)}{2}$ (returning to ground state $n_1=1 \implies N = \frac{n(n-1)}{2}$).

quickRevision: Balmer series (n₁=2) is the only series with lines in the visible region (400–700 nm).
